themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree that the huge spending by big tech companies on AI computing infrastructure is real and still growing, and that it is the main force driving stock market gains, with only a couple warning the rally could get ahead of itself if that spending slows.

facts_agreed.claim: Hyperscaler AI capex is large, still rising, and a key support for growth, earnings, and market leadership.
evidence_quotes: AI infrastructure continues to be built
AI capex remains one of the clearest supports for growth, earnings, and market leadership
2026 hyperscaler capex remains robust—revised 12% higher in Q1 to ~$720B
US hyperscalers’ March earnings confirmed that the AI capex upcycle is still in place
Hyperscaler capex looks set to grow by +90% in '26
realizing AI’s transformative potential would require an unprecedented level of capex
projected FY26 spending now greater than ~$685 billion
The AI investment cycle still appears to be at an early stage.

facts_agreed.claim: Corporate spending is shifting toward capex over buybacks, and investors are rewarding it.
evidence_quotes: We highlight an ongoing shift in corporate spending priorities toward capex over buybacks
Investors have recently preferred companies spending on capex and R&D.

facts_agreed.claim: Agentic AI is expected to drive a step-function jump in token demand that justifies the infrastructure spend.
evidence_quotes: Expect Agentic AI to drive a 24x jump in token demand

facts_contested.claim: whether the AI-driven rally is sustainable or markets are getting ahead of themselves
facts_contested.against_evidence: the longer the rally feeds on itself, the greater the risk that markets get too far ahead

themes.consensus_view: Banks broadly agree the Fed stays on hold this year with no rate cuts and a rate hike unlikely, while TS Lombard breaks from the pack arguing rates aren't actually high enough to slow the economy and markets will eventually have to price the Fed raising rates.

facts_agreed.claim: The Fed is not cutting rates this year and a hike looks unlikely, so policy stays on hold.
evidence_quotes: We no longer expect the Fed to cut rates this year.
we no longer expect the Fed to cut this year
we think Fed pricing is relatively fair
slowing wages and contained inflation expectations should keep the likelihood of a Fed hike low

facts_contested.claim: whether the bond market's current Fed pricing is correct
facts_contested.for_evidence: we think Fed pricing is relatively fair
facts_contested.against_evidence: The Fed and bond markets have yet to realise this

themes.consensus_view: The banks broadly agree the Federal Reserve has little reason to cut interest rates soon, with one expecting no cuts at all this year and others seeing no urgency given a still-decent jobs market.

facts_agreed.claim: There is currently no pressing need for the Fed to cut rates and easing policy will be hard to justify.
evidence_quotes: We expect no Fed cuts in 2026.
there is still no urgency to reduce rates to come to the aid
incoming Chair Kevin Warsh will have a hard time convincing his colleagues to ease policy

themes.consensus_view: Both banks are wary: the momentum trade (chasing what's already gone up, especially AI and semis) is overcrowded and overvalued, leaving it exposed to a sharp pullback if positioning unwinds.

facts_agreed.claim: Valuations are stretched and positioning in the momentum trade is at extremes, making it vulnerable to a sudden unwind.
evidence_quotes: optimism in the market may be starting to capitulate
Valuations are stretched, positioning in momentum is high
